title: The T-Gate Rule
lesson: A T gate restricts which Pauli checks can pass through it.
brief: This mirror circuit applies T and later undoes it with T†, so the ideal output is 000. Try to span the T gate with different Pauli checks and see which paths are allowed.
learning_moment: H, S, and CNOT are Clifford gates: they transform a Pauli into another Pauli, so the game can calculate a matching end edge. T is different. Z commutes with T and remains Z, but X or Y on that qubit generally becomes a combination of Paulis rather than one Pauli. This game's check must stay a single Pauli, so it allows a check to cross T or T† only when the propagated operator on that qubit is I or Z. This is a restriction on the check path, not a claim that the circuit itself cannot use T gates.
hint: Try spanning a T gate with X on q1, and read the notice (WHY? gives the full reason). Then find a path where the Pauli is Z (or I) at both T gates. You may need a check that starts on two qubits: drop a second piece in the same slot.
reflection: Which Pauli was present on the T qubit when the check crossed it?
noise_note: The model spreads errors across the gates using the same base rates.

explanation: Correct results are always 000. Both T gates are on q1, so the check must be Z or nothing on q1 when it passes them.

This check starts on two qubits after the first T gate: X on q0 and Z on q2. The CNOTs between q1 and q2 copy the Z onto q1 and then take it off again, so the check is nothing on q1 at the T† gate: legal.
It ends at the readout as Z on q0, q1 and q2.
